claims.text: Three-dimensional atom probe tomography can elucidate elemental redistribution associated with high-temperature oxidation in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Elemental redistribution at and around dual nanoprecipitates governs the formation of protective oxide layers.
Protective oxide formation associated with the nanoprecipitates affects the alloy's oxidation resistance.
The initial material is an additively manufactured, dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy.
Controlled high-temperature oxidation followed by 3D APT is the proposed investigative method.
An exposure range of 800–1000 °C is comparable to relevant gas-turbine or aerospace service conditions.
The nanoscale precipitates are likely Ni3Ti or Al–Ni-type phases.
Nanoprecipitates and their matrix interfaces play a pivotal role in elemental redistribution and oxide formation during high-temperature exposure.
Oxidation drives preferential diffusion of Cr, Al, and Ti toward nanoprecipitate interfaces.
APT can reveal local compositional gradients at nanoprecipitate and oxide interfaces.
Stable oxide layers form around precipitates and slow further oxidation advance.
APT will show distinct elemental concentration gradients at nanoprecipitate/oxide interfaces.
The interfacial concentration gradients will correlate with enhanced high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The additively manufactured alloy will have enhanced oxidation resistance relative to conventional cast or wrought counterparts.
Oxidation behavior in cast or wrought variants is only partially understood and lacks detailed three-dimensional nanoscale analysis of precipitate redistribution and oxide-formation sequences.
Temperature profiles, cyclic loading, and thermally induced changes in precipitate distribution may alter the results.
Limited data exist on oxidation-induced atomic-scale elemental redistribution in this alloy.
APT specimen preparation for this HEA composition may introduce reproducibility variability.
